title: A lasting research level in the state, value iteration on r15
result: rl-gate vs greedy-full-probe-perf-r15: (turn, level) PASS +152, with income PASS +158 (not significantly different); the (turn, level) policy also passes against static research x1.33 (+54) and x2 (+89): the timing pays; RL-line decision pending (David, Jakob)
question: With the research factor as a lasting level in the state, does value iteration find when to research more or less, and does that beat r15?
change: Experiment 29 with the action set research5 instead of econ5: the base bot's research factor (move type 0) at x0.5, x0.75, x1, x1.33 or x2, held between turns and moved one step at most per turn, from x1; value iteration over (turn, level) and (turn, level, income bucket).
method: 300k games with a random walk over the levels; value iteration for both state versions and min-count 20, 100, 500; min-count chosen per version on 2,000 validation seeds; both chosen policies on the 10,000 evaluation seeds against r15, and against the best fixed level of the action check if one beats r15
setups: Perfection, 16×16 continents, 4 players, Crazy, seat 0 Xin-Xi (human seat), learner base greedy-full-probe-perf-r15; opponents greedy-full-probe-perf-r15, greedy-full-probe-perf, greedy-full-probe-perf (anchor), seats shuffled per seed (rl-gate defaults from 27 Nov)
